Atlas is back but weak. Probing the actual harness endpoints.Now measuring the runtime instead of guessing. Checking the API container and the persisted run store size.Backend is fast when probed directly (list 22 ms, detail 424 ms, status 14 ms). So the failure is in the **view state**: `HarnessRunDetail` renders the "Select a harness task" empty state whenever `run` is null — including while the detail request is still in flight — and `HarnessView.refresh()` discards the whole list if `/harness/status` rejects. Fixing both.## What happened

- **Symptom**: the Harness view shows its "Select a harness task on the left to diagnose it." state even though the left list is loaded — no spinner, no error. It reads as "load tasks fails".
- **Measured the backend instead of guessing** (inside `codx-junior-api`, port 19980): `GET /api/orchestration` → **200 in 22 ms**, `GET /api/orchestration/{run}` → **200 in 424 ms**, `GET /api/harness/status` → **200 in 14 ms**. **Ruled out**: an API timeout / slow run list. The 11 runs on disk are small (2 KB–186 KB).
- **Confirmed in code**: the empty state is `v-if="!run"` with **no loading guard**, and `loadRun()` sets `run = null` on any error. So while the detail request is in flight (or after one transient failure) the panel claims "nothing is selected". `refresh()` wrapped status+list in `Promise.all`, so one failing call dropped the whole list.
- Side facts worth knowing: `.codx/harness/audit.jsonl` is already **2.9 MB** and is re-read every 10 s poll; socket.io polling showed **5.4 s** request times under load; a 39 MB `core` dump sits in the project root from Nov 13.

## What I did

- `client/src/components/harness/HarnessRunDetail.vue` — added a real loading state: spinner + "Loading the harness task…" while `!run && loading`; the "Select a harness task" placeholder now only appears when nothing is selected **and** there is no error.
- `client/src/views/HarnessView.vue` — `refresh()` now uses `Promise.allSettled`: a failing `/harness/status` no longer discards the run list and a failing run list no longer hides the health header; errors are surfaced instead of vanishing.
- `client/src/views/HarnessView.vue` — `loadRun()` keeps the last good payload on a transient error instead of blanking the diagnosis.
- **Not validated yet**: the QA gate (`qa_review_changes`) and no client build/type check ran — the tool budget closed before that.

## Demo

Reload the Harness view (`Harness` in the sidebar) and click through the 11 tasks: while a task loads you now see a spinner, and a failing poll shows a red alert while keeping the previous diagnosis.

## Next tasks

- `quick` — run the frontend gates on the two touched files: `qa_review_changes(paths=[client/src/views/HarnessView.vue, client/src/components/harness/HarnessRunDetail.vue], run_tests=false)` plus the client lint/build.
- `quick` — put a bounded axios timeout on `orchestration.get` in the view so a stalled request becomes an error instead of a permanent spinner.
- `max` — trim the poll cost: stop re-reading the 2.9 MB `audit.jsonl` on every 10 s tick (tail-read only the appended part), and investigate the 39 MB core dump + the 5.4 s socket.io latency.

**Good enough?** ok / next / what is wrong — `ok` ships it, `next` takes the first next task, `what is wrong` fixes this one.

modern AI harness works (durable runs, background workers, notifications,
audit trail) but it is built entirely inside codx-junior: no external harness,
no bridge, nothing to install.

## The @codx-junior profile

`codx-junior` is a **built-in profile** — the main contact between the user and
every other profile and capability of the platform. It is granted **all tools**
(the profile allowlist contains the `*` marker, expanded to the whole tool
registry at request time) and its `team` lists the profiles it can put to work:
`software_developer`, `analyst`, `reviewer`, `TaskManager`, `ProjectManager`,
`devops`, `repository`, `web_master`, `workspace`, `browser`, `wiki`,
`teacher` and `support`.

### Give it a task

1. Open any chat and write `@codx-junior <your task>`.
2. The harness profile registers the request (audited as `task_requested`) and
   decides how to run it:
   - quick, independent questions are answered directly or through a `delegate`
     card,
   - everything non-trivial becomes a **run** via
     `orchestrator(action="start")` with `profiles=["codx-junior"]`, so the
     harness profile itself supervises the work.
3. The background worker plans the steps and executes them **in parallel,
   isolated task cards**, each with the best profile for the job.
4. The user can watch every card live on the board and in the run sprint.
5. When the run finishes (or fails/stops/burns its budget), codx-junior
   publishes the **delivery report on the task** and sends the user a
   **notification**: *"Run X finished (completed). The delivery report is on
   the task."* The notification is sent exactly once per terminal status, even
   across worker restarts.

## Observability: navigate and review everything

- **Every step is a task card.** Open a card to read the worker conversation,
  move it, retry it or take over manually.
- **The run sprint** groups all the cards of a run by status.
- **The Harness app** (sidebar → *Harness*) shows, per project:
  - the worker heartbeat and watchdog state (restarts, incidents),
  - every run with status, progress, board/sprint, budget and a one-click
    *Open task* link to the run dashboard,
  - the full **audit journal** (see below), filterable by event type.

## Audit: all work is registered

Everything the harness does is appended to an immutable journal at
`<project>/.codx/harness/audit.jsonl` (one JSON object per line, atomic
appends):

| Event | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `task_requested` | the user gave `@codx-junior` a task (chat, user, request text) |
| `run_event` | every run transition: `run_created`, `run_started`, `step_started`, `step_finished`, `step_retried`, `run_completed`, `run_failed`, `run_stopped`, `run_budget_exhausted`, `run_stalled`, `report`, … with run id, status and message |
| `notification_sent` | the user was notified of a terminal status |
| `turn_resumed` / `turn_recovered` | an interrupted chat turn was resumed by the recovery worker (attempt n/m) and completed |
| `turn_failed` / `turn_cancelled` | an interrupted turn was given up after the retry bound (the user is notified), or stopped by the user |
| `worker_recovered` | the background worker (re)started and took over a project |
| `worker_stalled` | the watchdog detected a dead/wedged worker with active runs |
| `worker_restarted` / `worker_restart_failed` | supervision actions and their outcome |
